questions.question_text: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides of $6$ cm (original) and $21$ cm (image). The original triangle has a perimeter of $16$ cm. What is the perimeter of the image?

options.why: Applied the scale factor twice — that is how area scales, but perimeter is a length and scales by the factor once.
Added the $15$ cm difference between the given sides to $16$; the perimeter is multiplied by the scale factor, not increased by a fixed amount.
Assumed the perimeter is unchanged; every side is multiplied by $3.5$, so the perimeter is too.

questions.solution_text:
$k=\frac{\text{image}}{\text{original}}=\frac{21}{6}=3.5$
Every side is multiplied by $3.5$, so the perimeter is too.
$P=16\times3.5$
$=56\text{ cm}$
